source_text: Est exterior homo et interior. Exterioris membra manifesta sunt; interioris quoque membra describuntur in Scripturis: oculos cordis, aures interiores, manus animae. Canticum Canticorum non de exteriore carnali amore loquitur, sed de interiore, quo anima Verbum amat. Nisi quis se noverit interiorem, nescit quid in hoc libro quaerat; alioquin verba nuptialia scandalum faciunt.
pass_a_gloss: There-is outer human and inner. Of-outer members manifest are; of-inner also members are-described in Scriptures... Song of-Songs not about outer carnal love speaks, but about inner, by-which soul Word loves...
pass_b_english: There is an outer human and an inner. The members of the outer are plain; the members of the inner are also described in the Scriptures — eyes of the heart, inner ears, hands of the soul. The Song of Songs does not speak of outer carnal love, but of the inner love by which the soul loves the Word. Unless someone knows himself or herself as inner, that person does not know what to seek in this book; otherwise the bridal words become a scandal.
